text: Find the values of $k$ for which the equation $(k+1)x^{2}-2(k-1)x+1=0$ has equal roots. For each value of $k$, find the repeated root.
The roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of the equation $x^{2}-9x+k=0$ satisfy $\alpha-2\beta=3$. Find the value of $k$.
If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^{2}-5x+2=0$, form the quadratic equation whose roots are $\alpha^{2}$ and $\beta^{2}$.
The code of a school locker is a two-digit number. The product of its digits is 14, and when 45 is added to the number, its digits get interchanged. Find the code.
Find two consecutive positive even integers the sum of whose squares is 340.
The sum of two numbers is 15 and the sum of their reciprocals is $\frac{3}{10}$. Find the numbers.
The sum of the areas of two squares is $468\text{ m}^{2}$ and the sum of their perimeters is 120 m. Find the sides of the two squares.
Two taps together fill a school's rainwater storage tank in 6 hours. Working alone, one tap takes 5 hours more than the other to fill it. Find the time each tap takes alone.
A school spends ₹720 on buying potted plants of the same kind. If each plant had cost ₹6 less, the school could have bought 4 more plants for the same money. Find the cost of one plant.
A shopkeeper sells a table lamp for ₹75 and makes a profit percent equal to the cost price of the lamp in rupees. Find the cost price of the lamp.
Solve for $x$: $\frac{1}{x-3}+\frac{2}{x-2}=\frac{8}{x}$, where $x\ne 0, 2, 3$.
Solve for $x$: $\frac{1}{3a+b+3x}=\frac{1}{3a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{3x}$, where $x\ne 0$ and $3a+b+3x\ne 0$.
Find the least positive value of $p$ for which the equation $x^{2}+2(p-1)x+(p+5)=0$ has real roots. Hence solve the equation for that value of $p$.
A motorcyclist covers 120 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 8 km/h more, the journey would have taken 30 minutes less. Find the original speed and the time taken at that speed.
A cyclist rides the first 24 km of a trip at a uniform speed and the next 30 km at a speed 2 km/h less than before. The whole trip takes 5 hours. Find the speed for the first part of the trip.
An express bus and an ordinary bus both cover a distance of 360 km. The express bus is 15 km/h faster and takes 2 hours less than the ordinary bus. Find the speeds of the two buses.

An aircraft took off 1 hour late from its scheduled time. To reach its destination 3000 km away on time, the pilot had to increase the usual speed by 250 km/h. Find the usual speed of the aircraft and the scheduled duration of the flight.

A cyclist rides 36 km uphill to a hill-top village and returns along the same road at a speed 6 km/h more than the uphill speed. The uphill ride takes 1 hour longer than the return ride. Find the uphill and downhill speeds.
The sum of the areas of two squares is $544\text{ m}^{2}$ and the difference of their perimeters is 32 m. Find the sides of the two squares.

A circular park has a diameter $AB$ of length 26 m, with gates at $A$ and $B$. A lamp post is to be fixed at a point $P$ on the boundary of the park so that the distance of the post from gate $B$ is 14 m more than its distance from gate $A$. Find the distances $PA$ and $PB$, and the area of $\triangle APB$.

text: Three years ago, a mother's age was twice the square of her daughter's age. Five years from now, the mother's age will be 4 more than three times the daughter's age then. Find their present ages.

The numerator of a fraction is 3 less than its denominator. If 2 is added to both the numerator and the denominator, the sum of the new fraction and the original fraction is $\frac{26}{21}$. Find the original fraction.

Ravi's marks in Mathematics and Science in a class test add up to 30. Had he scored 2 marks more in Mathematics and 3 marks less in Science, the product of his marks would have been 210. Find his marks in the two subjects.

A tailor bought a roll of cloth for ₹1800. Had the cloth been ₹10 per metre cheaper, he would have got 6 m more cloth for the same amount. Find the length of the roll and the original price per metre.

A housing society has a rectangular lawn 20 m long and 14 m wide. It decides to build a walkway of uniform width $x$ m all around the outside of the lawn. The lawn and the walkway together cover an area of $432\text{ m}^{2}$. The cost of paving the walkway will depend on its area.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Write the equation in $x$ for the total area of the lawn and the walkway.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Write this equation in the standard form $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$ with the simplest whole-number coefficients.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the width of the walkway and the area of the walkway.

text: A student has a photograph 15 cm long and 10 cm wide. She wants a print in which both the length and the width are increased by the same amount $x$ cm, so that the area of the print is double the area of the original photograph.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Form the quadratic equation in $x$ for the doubled area.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the length and width of the new print.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: If instead the area were to be tripled, would $x$ be a rational number? Justify your answer.

text: A square classroom floor is to be covered completely with identical square tiles. Using tiles of side $x$ cm, exactly 225 tiles are needed. If tiles 6 cm longer in side are used instead, exactly 144 tiles are needed.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Form a quadratic equation in $x$ by equating the area of the floor in the two cases.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the side of the smaller tile.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the side and the area of the floor, in metres and square metres.

text: A delivery van covers a 200 km route every day at a uniform speed of $x$ km/h. The manager notices that if the van were driven 10 km/h faster, the trip would take 1 hour less.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the discriminant of this equation and state the nature of its roots.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the usual speed of the van and the time it takes for the route.

text: A school wants to rope off a rectangular play area on its ground using exactly 36 m of rope for the boundary. The breadth of the area is $x$ m. The sports teacher first asks for an area of $85\text{ m}^{2}$; if that is not possible, the plan is revised to an area of $77\text{ m}^{2}$.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Express the area of the play area in terms of $x$.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Can the area be $85\text{ m}^{2}$? Justify using the discriminant.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the length and breadth for the revised area of $77\text{ m}^{2}$.
